issues.acceptance: A representative native-renderer before/after capture reports raw frame times, one-percent low, hitch count, CPU/GPU attribution, and named script hot paths with 3, 5, 10, and 18 active enemies. Enemy separation is computed once from a cached stable roster per physics cycle, QA instrumentation performs no per-frame deep state snapshot or scene-wide scan in ordinary play, and AI behavior/spacing remains unchanged. llvmpipe evidence is recorded only as collector evidence.
issues.actual: scripts/enemy_agent.gd rebuilds and sorts the complete fusepoint_enemy group inside _separation_safe_velocity(), then invokes that admission path multiple times per navigation cycle for every active enemy. At the same time, the main scene runs RuntimeQualificationProbe in PROCESS_MODE_ALWAYS, deep-calls mission/roster/weapon state and periodically scans the complete scene tree for audio players. With 18 active enemies these are credible CPU hitch hot paths and must be profiled on a native renderer; the llvmpipe collector result cannot attribute the user's stutter to their computer.
issues.expected: Ordinary gameplay performs bounded enemy steering and lightweight production work per frame; deep QA snapshots run only on demand or at a bounded debug sampling cadence.
issues.next_action: Capture native-renderer CPU/GPU profiler evidence, remove duplicate peer scans and sorts, and gate or sample QA-only deep observation.

blocking_focus: Complete the candidate-bound Tester MCP state matrix.

preservation_constraints.requirement: Keep frozen technical baseline `clean_boot` passing. Do not treat this as a mandate to preserve the same visible asset, map, HUD family, or material choice if a higher-quality replacement is available and the PRD still fits.

task_specification.objective: Make the three selected combat-readability issues closure-ready by restoring the accepted enemy rifle wrapper exactly, rebuilding loadout selection around recognizable weapon imagery, and repairing localized Alpha-route highlight clipping while preserving all accepted component and runtime baselines.

diagnosis.root_cause: The enemy regression is localized to direct-instance wrapper binding, attachment lifecycle, or pose-to-socket synchronization for soldier_b, not to the accepted Loop 66 aim/action overlays. The loadout remains a text-led pair of repeated Button cards without visual weapon identity. The required global daylight tuple is already bound, so Alpha-route clipping must be isolated at the affected material, import, or localized lighting boundary rather than addressed with another global exposure adjustment.

stop_conditions: Do not replace, split, or edit the retained humanoid, rifle, viewmodel, audio, or authored map source packages.
Do not remove or alter the accepted Loop 66 _apply_rifle_aim_overlay and _apply_rifle_action_overlay calls or their bone rotations.
Do not change the registered global daylight tuple, sky, shadows, SSAO, cloud bindings, directional flare, or sun energy to hide the localized Alpha defect.
Do not claim enemy repair from source constants, clip names, or telemetry alone; matched living runtime frames and state receipts for both skins are required.
Keep implementation limited to the three selected issue IDs. Deferred input, audio, and performance issues receive regression patrol only.
Stop after focused Developer self-validation; GameLoop Runtime and Tester own formal recapture, issue closure, and phase verdicts.

strategy.rationale: Use a new root-cause strategy after the plateau: restore and isolate the accepted direct enemy instance lifecycle without transform tuning, replace the loadout's text-card composition rather than restyling it, and repair only the proven localized highlight boundary while freezing the accepted environment.

code: Run focused script/resource validation and the frozen clean_boot check after all repairs; require successful parsing/import, intact bindings, and no editor errors.
Confirm exactly one enemy socket/rifle/muzzle instance per actor, deterministic lifecycle cleanup, preserved overlay call order and bone rotations, and unchanged imported character/rifle sources.
Inspect loadout bindings so focus, selection, confirmation, equipped ID, ammunition, fire mode, and visible viewmodel remain one authoritative chain.

Confirm exact retained environment values and unchanged imported map source bindings, then reread editor and runtime errors after animation, loadout, traversal, firing, reload, pause/resume, and recovery callbacks.
runtime: GameLoop Runtime and Tester first run one ordinary-input boot and deployment smoke covering physical G one-step briefing skip, captured horizontal and vertical mouse look, W movement, pause/resume capture, R reload-only behavior, and F6 recovery.

Tester uses the stable non-release enemy preparation fixture and matched state/frame sampling for both skins across idle, walk, run, aim, fire, reload, a 60-second delayed pre-objective state, recovery, and checkpoint restore; preparation must not advance the encounter.

Tester opens the loadout with keyboard, mouse, and gamepad at 100 percent, changes focus and selection between both weapons, confirms each through deployment, repeats the 200 percent stress probe, restores 100 percent through settings, and verifies persistence after restart.

Tester traverses to the same Alpha-route viewpoint and pairs framebuffer evidence with runtime environment/material state for sunlit and shaded concrete, verifying the exact tuple and preserved atmospheric layers together rather than accepting telemetry or an unbound screenshot alone.
visual: Compare enemy adjacent frames for both skins, emphasizing right-hand socket stability, left-hand/foregrip relationship, stock/shoulder readability, muzzle-forward alignment, accepted aim/action overlays, upright hips, planted feet, and clean fire/reload recovery.

Capture AK-focused, Saiga-focused, and selected loadout states at 1280x720 and 1920x1080 at 100 percent and at 1280x720 at 200 percent; reject text-only identity, repeated card shells, clipping, unclear focus, stale selection, or unbound imagery.

Capture the repaired Alpha route using the reproduction framing plus one shaded comparison; reject lost texture detail, near-white highlight plateaus, material seams, color contamination, or loss of atmospheric composition.
Finish with persisted fullscreen enabled, actual window and viewport 1920x1080, content scale 1.0, 3D render scale 1.0, and restored persisted 100 percent UI scale.

done_when: The enemy presentation wrapper uses one stable direct rifle instance per living actor, with deterministic teardown/rebind behavior across skin initialization, activation, checkpoint restore, and reuse; no stale or duplicate WeaponSocket, PrimaryRifle, source, or muzzle instance survives a rebind.

The accepted Loop 66 tuple remains exact: rifle source position (0,-4.8,5), socket position (0.02,0.02,-0.02), socket rotation (-90,90,0), authored local PI roll, unchanged skin scales, right-hand attachment, and no per-frame socket, hand-teleport, or stock-height compensation.

The pose pipeline explicitly retains _apply_rifle_aim_overlay and _apply_rifle_action_overlay after retargeting. Aim preserves spine_mid/right-axis 0.18, chest/right-axis 0.34, and both shoulder/right-axis 0.20 pitch weights. Fire preserves chest/right-axis -3.5 degrees, right-shoulder/up-axis -2.0 degrees, and left-shoulder/up-axis -1.25 degrees at pulse peak. Reload preserves left-shoulder/fore!

Matched living runtime frames and state receipts for soldier_a and soldier_b cover idle, walk, run, aim, fire, reload, delayed play, and recovery; both hands remain credibly associated with the rifle, stock and shoulder contact reads coherently, the muzzle points forward, hips remain upright, and feet remain grounded.

Every living actor with nonzero horizontal velocity uses an upright locomotion-compatible pose; no unarmed, pistol-like, prone, death, hit-terminal, detached-weapon, grounded-body, or transform-only substitute appears.

The stable combat preparation fixture ends in an inspectable living state with requested, resolved, generation, branch, and reset-isolation receipts; it does not kill actors, capture an objective, or advance the encounter and has no release-build binding.

AI, perception, navigation, firing authority, damage, spawn, lifecycle, and telemetry behavior remains unchanged; internal pistol-named source clips do not fail acceptance when matched rendered behavior passes.
